slides.0.title: Regulatory change and Diploma essays
slides.0.subtitle: From piecemeal rules to layered tiers, and an essay template
slides.1.title: Regulatory timeline
slides.1.highlights.0.title: 1909 to 1948
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Armagnac's designation decreed 1909; Jurançon, Monbazillac, Bergerac 1936; Duras and Montravel 1937; Gaillac white 1938; Pécharmant and Rosette 1946; Madiran 1948
slides.1.highlights.1.title: 1970 to 1995
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Irouléguy and Gaillac red 1970; Cahors 1971; Buzet 1973; Béarn and Jurançon Sec 1975; Marcillac and Marmandais 1990; Côtes de Bergerac 1995
slides.1.highlights.2.title: 2005 to 2011
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Saussignac 2005; the IGP renaming in 2009; Saint-Mont and Tursan 2011
slides.1.content: The order of promotions reflects when each area revived.
slides.2.title: From Vin de Pays to IGP
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The Côtes de Gascogne path
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Wikipedia: a decree of 13 September 1968 separated Vin de Pays from table wine; the producers' association was founded on 15 March 1979; a decree of 25 January 1982 introduced stricter standards
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Legislation dates differ
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Wine With Seth says Vin de Pays legislation followed in 1973 and was passed in 1979, which differs from Wikipedia's 1968 / 1979 account, so legislation years are not tested
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The 2009 renaming
slides.2.highlights.2.content: From 1 August 2009 all Vin de Pays were renamed IGP under EU 607/2009 (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.content: IGP is the EU-style renaming of Vin de Pays.
slides.3.title: Evolving specification details
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Tannat in Madiran
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The first 1948 decree required 20 months of barrel ageing (wein.plus); today Tannat must be at least 60% of each estate's vineyard and oak ageing is not mandatory
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Gaillac Doux
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The former names Liquoreux and Moelleux are no longer authorised; the style is now Doux with at least 70 g/L (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Pacherenc's 2005 change
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Rules changed in 2005: previously a set share of Arrufiac was required and Sémillon was permitted (Wikipedia)
slides.3.content: Specifications are adjusted as positioning changes.
slides.4.title: Essay template
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Thesis: diversity as identity
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Open with: the South-West is a collection of Dordogne, Lot, Tarn, Gascony and Pyrenean districts, not one style; support with "native varieties + valley terroirs"
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Evidence: history and system
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Bordeaux's police des vins held the region back, AOCs were promoted at different times (1936–2011) and IGP gives freedom; cite specific years
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Conclusion: value and positioning
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Conclude on the market: cooperatives and volume IGP exports, the distinct AOC styles, sweet wines and spirits, noting that area sources disagree
slides.4.content: The most convincing essays cite year, specification figure and source.
In which year was the Armagnac designation decreed (wein.plus)?
On what date did the decree introducing stricter standards for Côtes de Gascogne vin de pays come?
When were all Vin de Pays renamed IGP?
How long a barrel ageing did Madiran's first 1948 decree require?
Which old names did Gaillac Doux replace?
D. Rancio and Vin de Voile
Those two old names are no longer authorised.
What makes an essay most convincing?
A. Year, specification figure and source
